title: Gullak Season 5 Drops Tomorrow. The Show That Understood the Indian Middle Class Better Than Anyone Is Back.
excerpt: TVF's beloved Mishra family returns on SonyLIV with a new Annu, a mother discovering the internet, and the quiet drama of growing up and away from home.
body:
If you have ever lived in a two-bedroom flat where the WiFi password was a family event, Gullak already knows your story.

The Viral Fever's quiet masterpiece returns for its fifth season on SonyLIV tomorrow, June 5, and the Mishra family is doing what Indian families do best: changing just enough to stay exactly the same.

## What Has Changed

The biggest shift this season is structural. Anant V. Joshi takes over the role of Anand "Annu" Mishra, the elder son, replacing the actor who carried the part through four seasons. Recasting a lead in a show built entirely on familiarity is a bold move, and early reports suggest the transition is handled with care rather than glossed over. Annu is now dealing with career pressures, self-doubt, and the very Indian anxiety of proving yourself while your parents watch.

Aman, played by Harsh Mayar, returns from college more mature and carrying his own set of secrets. The younger Mishra brother has grown up between seasons, and the show appears to be letting that growth breathe rather than freezing him in place.

Then there is Shanti Mishra, played by Geetanjali Kulkarni, arguably the show's emotional center. This season, Shanti gains an online identity — a plotline that any NRI who has watched their mother discover WhatsApp groups and YouTube will recognize instantly. It is funny because it is true, and Gullak has always understood that truth is where the comedy lives.

Santosh Mishra, played by Jameel Khan, introduces modern upgrades to Mishra Niwas, including WiFi. For a household where every small expenditure was a family debate, the arrival of the internet is not a tech upgrade — it is a cultural event.

Shanti's brother Pinky, played by Gopal Datt, arrives for a visit, adding a new dynamic to the household. Sunita Rajwar and Helly Shah also join the cast this season. The directors are Shreyansh Pandey and Abhay Raut, continuing the show's tradition of quiet, observational storytelling.

## Why Gullak Matters

There is no shortage of Indian family dramas on streaming platforms. What makes Gullak different — and what has made it different since its first season in 2019 — is its refusal to exaggerate. The Mishras are not dysfunctional for laughs. They are not aspirational for drama. They are middle-class in the way that most Indians actually are: careful with money, loud about love, quietly ambitious, and fundamentally decent.

Jameel Khan, who plays Santosh, put it simply in a recent interview: "This is the biggest class in the world. It is important to represent it in a fun and relatable way." He is right. The Indian middle class has been either mocked or mythologized on screen for decades. Gullak just observes it.

## The Diaspora Connection

For Indians living abroad, Gullak is not comfort viewing — it is memory viewing. The cramped living room, the mother's running commentary on everyone's life choices, the father's quiet pride, the brothers who fight over nothing and would die for each other. If you grew up in a Mishra Niwas of your own, every episode of Gullak feels like a phone call home.

Season 5 appears to be engaging directly with the experience of outgrowing one's roots — Annu possibly moving out, Aman returning changed, the parents adjusting to a household that is evolving without their permission. For anyone in the diaspora who has navigated the guilt of growing away from home while growing up in it, this season's themes will land hard.

Five episodes. The Mishra family. No explosions, no plot twists, no villain. Just the quiet drama of being alive in an Indian household. That has always been enough.

Gullak Season 5 streams on SonyLIV from June 5, 2026.
